You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace
</RULES>

# Bartib

Bartib is an easy to use time tracking tool for the command line. It saves a log of all tracked activities as a plaintext file and allows you to create flexible reports.

Usage examples

Start a new activity:

  bartib start -d "Description of the activity" -p "Project Name"

Stop the running activity:

  bartib stop

Continue the most recent activity:

  bartib continue

List today's activities:

  bartib list --today

Report for today:

  bartib report --today

Configuration

Bartib records activities in a plaintext log file. You can either pass the file explicitly with the -f/--file option, or set the BARTIB_FILE environment variable to point to your log file. Example:

  export BARTIB_FILE="/home/username/activities.bartib"

If the file does not exist, Bartib will create it when you start tracking.

Installation

Download a prebuilt executable from the project's releases and place it in a directory on your PATH (for example: ~/bin). Bartib may also be available through your distribution's package manager.

Autocompletion

Completion scripts for shells may be provided in the repository's misc/ directory. Source the appropriate script for your shell to enable completion of project and task names.

#compdef bartib

_bartib_tasks() {
    local -a _tasks=($(bartib last | head -n -1 | awk 'BEGIN { a="" } NR > 2 {for (i=2; i <= NF - 1; i++) { if (i != 2) { a=a" "$i; } else { a=$i } } gsub("[\[\]]", "", $1); printf("%s[%s]\n", $1, a)}' | tr '\n' ' '))

    _values "TASK" ${_tasks[@]}
}

_bartib_projects() {
    local -a _projects=($(bartib projects --no-quotes | sort | tr '\n' ' '))

    _values "PROJECTS" ${_projects[@]}
}

_bartib() {
    typeset -A opt_args
    local context state line
    local current_context="${curcontext}"

    _arguments -C \
        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[Prints help information]' \
        '(-v --version)'{-v,--version}'[Prints version information]' \
        '-f[the file in which bartib tracks all the activities]:FILE:_files' \
        '1:bartib commands:->commands' \
        '*:: :->command_arguments'

    case $state in
        commands)
            local commands
            commands=(
                'cancel:cancels all currently running activities',
                'change:changes the current activity',
                'check:checks file and reports parsing errors',
                'continue:continues a previous activity',
                'current:lists all currently running activities',
                'edit:opens the activity log in an editor',
                'help:Prints this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)',
                'last:displays the descriptions and projects of recent activities',
                'list:list recent activities',
                'projects:list all projects',
                'report:reports duration of tracked activities',
                'sanity:checks sanity of bartib log',
                'search:search for existing descriptions and projects',
                'start:starts a new activity',
                'status:shows current status and time reports for today, current week, and current month',
                'stop:stops all currently running activities'
            )
            _describe -t commands 'bartib command' commands
            ;;

        command_arguments)
            case $words[1] in
                cancel)
                    _arguments -C \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[Prints help information]'
                    ;;
                change)
                    _arguments -C \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[Prints help information]' \
                        '(-d --description)'{-d,--description}'[the description of the new activity]:DESCRIPTION:()' \
                        '(-p,--project)'{-p,--project}'[the project to which the new activity belongs]:PROJECT:_bartib_projects' \
                        '(-t,--time)'{-t,--time}'[the time for changing the activity status (HH:MM)]:TIME:()'
                    ;;
                check)
                    _arguments -C \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[Prints help information]'
                    ;;
                continue)
                    _arguments -C \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[Prints help information]' \
                        '(-d --description)'{-d,--description}'[the description of the new activity]:DESCRIPTION:()' \
                        '(-p --project)'{-p,--project}'[the project to which the new activity belongs]:PROJECT:_bartib_projects' \
                        '(-t --time)'{-t,--time}'[the time for changing the activity status (HH:MM)]:TIME:()' \
                        '*::NUMBER:_bartib_tasks'
                    ;;
                help)
                    _arguments \
                        '*::SUBCOMMAND:(cancel change check continue current edit help last list projects report sanity search start status stop)'
                    ;;
                list)
                    _arguments -C \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[Prints help information]' \
                        '(--current-week)'--current-week'[show activities of the current week]' \
                        '(--last-week)'--last-week'[show activities of the last week]' \
                        '(--no_grouping)'--no_grouping'[do not group activities by date in list]' \
                        '(--today)'--today'[show activities of the current day]' \
                        '(--yesterday)'--yesterday"[show yesterdays' activities]" \
                        '(-d --date)'{-d,--date}'[show activities of a certain date only]:DATE:' \
                        '(--from)'--from'[begin of date range (inclusive)]:DATE:' \
                        '(--n --number)'{-n,--number}'[maximum number of activities to display]:NUMBER:' \
                        '(--p --project)'{-p,--project}'[do list activities for this project only]:PROJECT:_bartib_projects' \
                        '(--round)'--round'[rounds the start and end time to the nearest duration. Durations can be in minutes or hours. E.g. 15m or 4h]:ROUND:' \
                        '(--to)'--to'[end of date range (inclusive)]:TO_DATE:'
                    ;;
                projects)
                    _arguments -C \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[Prints help information]' \
                        '(-c --current)'{-c,--current}'[prints currently running projects only]' \
                        '(-n --no-quotes)'{-n,--no-quotes}'[prints projects without quotes]'
                    ;;
                report)
                    _arguments -C \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[Prints help information]' \
                        '(--current_week)'--current_week'[show activities of the current week]' \
                        '(--last_week)'--last_week'[show activities of the last week]' \
                        '(--today)'--today'[show activities of the current day]' \
                        '(--yesterday)'--yesterday"[show yesterdays' activities]" \
                        '(-d --date)'{-d,--date}'[show activities of a certain date only]:DATE:' \
                        '(--from)'--from'[begin of date range (inclusive)]:DATE:' \
                        '(-p --project)'{-p,--project}'[do report activities for this project only]:PROJECT:_bartib_projects' \
                        '(--round)'--round'[rounds the start and end time to the nearest duration. Durations can be in minutes or hours. E.g. 15m or 4h]:ROUND:' \
                        '(--to)'--to'[end of date range (inclusive)]:DATE:'
                    ;;
                sanity)
                    _arguments -C \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[Prints help information]'
                    ;;
                search)
                    _arguments -C \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[Prints help information]' \
                        '*::SEARCH_TERM:'
                    ;;
                start)
                    _arguments -C \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[Prints help information]' \
                        '(-d --description)'{-d,--description}'[the description of the new activity]:DESCRIPTION:()' \
                        '(-p,--project)'{-p,--project}'[the project to which the new activity belongs]:PROJECT:_bartib_projects' \
                        '(-t,--time)'{-t,--time}'[the time for changing the activity status (HH:MM)]:TIME:()'
                    ;;
                stop)
                    _arguments -C \
                        '(-h --help)'{-h,--help}'[show command line help]' \
                        '(-t,--time)'{-t,--time}'[the time for changing the activity status (HH:MM)]:TIME:()'
                    ;;
            esac
            ;;
    esac
}

_bartib "${@}"

		COMPREPLY=()
	else

def escape_text(s):
    # escape backslash then pipe
    # replace \ with \\ then | with \|
    return s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("|", "\\|")

def split_escaped_pipe(line):
    # split on unescaped |
    segs = []
    cur = []
    i = 0
    n = len(line)
    while i < n:
        c = line[i]
        if c == "\\":
            if i+1 < n:
                cur.append(line[i+1])
                i += 2
            else:
                i += 1
        elif c == "|":
            segs.append(''.join(cur).strip())
            cur = []
            i += 1
        else:
            cur.append(c)
            i += 1
    segs.append(''.join(cur).strip())
    return segs

def parse_datetime_str(s):
    try:
        # format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
        return dt.strptime(s, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
    except:
        return None

def format_datetime(d):
    return d.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")

def format_time(d):
    return d.strftime("%H:%M")

def format_duration(minutes):
    if minutes < 1:
        return "<1m"
    hours = minutes // 60
    mins = minutes % 60
    if hours == 0:
        return f"{mins:02d}m"
    else:
        return f"{hours}h {mins:02d}m"

def parse_date_str(s):
    # try YYYY-MM-DD
    try:
        return dt.strptime(s, "%Y-%m-%d").date()
    except:
        return None

def parse_time_arg(s):
    # returns datetime for today or None + error type
    # check contains invalid characters: if not matches pattern \d{1,2}:\d{2}
    # Actually check if string matches ^\d{1,2}:\d{2}$ else invalid characters
    if not re.match(r'^\d{1,2}:\d{2}$', s):
        return None, "invalid_chars"
    h, m = s.split(":")
    try:
        hi = int(h); mi = int(m)
    except:
        return None, "invalid_chars"
    if hi <0 or hi>23 or mi<0 or mi>59:
        return None, "out_of_range"
    # construct today datetime
    today = ddate.today()
    # use local now? We'll use today's date
    try:
        return dt.combine(today, dtime(hi, mi)), None
    except:
        return None, "out_of_range"

def parse_duration_str(s):
    # expects number + m or h
    if len(s) < 2:
        return None
    suffix = s[-1]
    if suffix not in ('m','h'):
        return None
    num = s[:-1]
    if not num.isdigit():
        return None
    try:
        n = int(num)
    except:
        return None
    if suffix == 'm':
        return n
    else:
        return n*60

def round_datetime(d, round_minutes):
    if round_minutes is None or round_minutes == 0:
        return d
    # compute minutes since midnight
    minutes = d.hour*60 + d.minute
    # round to nearest
    # using half up
    rounded = int(minutes / round_minutes + 0.5) * round_minutes
    # handle overflow to next day
    days_add = rounded // 1440
    rounded_minutes = rounded % 1440
    new_hour = rounded_minutes // 60
    new_min = rounded_minutes % 60
    new_date = d.date() + timedelta(days=days_add)
    # preserve seconds 0
    return dt.combine(new_date, dtime(new_hour, new_min))

def handle_report(file_path, args):

    date_filter=None

                date_filter=d

            if i+1>=len(args):
                error_subcommand_usage("report", f"error: The argument '{a} <FROM_DATE>' requires a value but none was supplied")
            val=args[i+1]
            d=parse_date_str(val)
            if d is None:
                stdout_write(f'Can not parse "{val}" as date. Argument for --from is ignored (input contains invalid characters)\n')
            else:

            i+=2

            if i+1>=len(args):
                error_subcommand_usage("report", f"error: The argument '{a} <TO_DATE>' requires a value but none was supplied")
            val=args[i+1]
            d=parse_date_str(val)
            if d is None:
                stdout_write(f'Can not parse "{val}" as date. Argument for --to is ignored (input contains invalid characters)\n')
            else:
                to_date=d
            i+=2
        elif a in ("-p","--project"):
            if i+1>=len(args):
                error_subcommand_usage("report", f"error: The argument '{a} <PROJECT>' requires a value but none was supplied")
            project_filter=args[i+1]; i+=2
        elif a=="--round":
            if i+1>=len(args):
                error_subcommand_usage("report", f"error: The argument '{a} <round>' requires a value but none was supplied")
            val=args[i+1]
            rm=parse_duration_str(val)
            if rm is None:
                stdout_write(f'Can not parse "{val}" as duration. Argument for --round is ignored\n')
            else:
                round_minutes=rm
            i+=2
        elif a in ("-h","--help"):
            stdout_write(HELP_REPORT)
            sys.exit(0)
        elif a.startswith("-"):
            error_subcommand_usage("report", f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context")
        else:
            error_subcommand_usage("report", f"error: Found argument '{a}' which wasn't expected, or isn't valid in this context")
    file_path=ensure_file_arg(file_path)
    acts, errs, err = read_file(file_path)
    if err=="not_found":
        eprint(f"Error: Could not read from file: {file_path}\n\nCaused by:\n    No such file or directory (os error 2)\n")
        sys.exit(1)
    elif err:
        eprint(f"Error: Could not read from file: {file_path}\n\nCaused by:\n    {err}\n")
        sys.exit(1)
    for line_no, line, typ in errs:
        stdout_write(f"Warning: Ignoring line {line_no}. Please see `bartib check` for further information\n")
    if errs:
        stdout_write("\n")
    # filtering
    filtered=[]
    today_date=ddate.today()
    yesterday_date=today_date - timedelta(days=1)
    monday_current = today_date - timedelta(days=today_date.weekday())
    sunday_current = monday_current + timedelta(days=6)
    monday_last = monday_current - timedelta(days=7)
    sunday_last = monday_current - timedelta(days=1)
    for act in acts:
        if project_filter is not None and act["project"] != project_filter:
            continue
        act_date=act["start"].date()
        if date_filter is not None:
            if act_date != date_filter: continue
        else:
            if today and act_date != today_date: continue
            if yesterday and act_date != yesterday_date: continue
            if current_week and not (monday_current <= act_date <= sunday_current): continue
            if last_week and not (monday_last <= act_date <= sunday_last): continue
            if from_date is not None and act_date < from_date: continue
            if to_date is not None and act_date > to_date: continue
        filtered.append(act)
    # compute durations with rounding
    now=get_now()
    # aggregate
    # map project -> dict description -> minutes
    proj_desc_minutes={}
    total_by_proj={}
    total_all=0
    for act in filtered:
        start_dt = round_datetime(act["start"], round_minutes) if round_minutes else act["start"]
        if act["end"] is not None:
            end_dt = round_datetime(act["end"], round_minutes) if round_minutes else act["end"]
            diff=end_dt - start_dt
        else:
            now_r=round_datetime(now, round_minutes) if round_minutes else now
            diff=now_r - start_dt
        mins=int(diff.total_seconds()//60)
        if mins<0: mins=0
        proj=act["project"]
        desc=act["description"]
        if proj not in proj_desc_minutes:
            proj_desc_minutes[proj]={}
            total_by_proj[proj]=0
        if desc not in proj_desc_minutes[proj]:
            proj_desc_minutes[proj][desc]=0
        proj_desc_minutes[proj][desc]+=mins
        total_by_proj[proj]+=mins
        total_all+=mins
    # handle empty: if filtered empty, then no project lines, but total still <1m ?
    # According to earlier, empty filtered for report with --last_week gave Total <1m
    # And list gave No activity
    # So report always prints total even if no activities? Let's check for empty file: report gave Total <1m
    # So we should print total even if no projects
    # Compute width for dots: need max length among all project names, description names plus indent
    # width = max( len(project), len(desc)+4, len("Total") )
    # We'll compute
    all_names=[]
    for proj, descs in proj_desc_minutes.items():
        all_names.append(proj)
        for desc in descs:
            all_names.append("    "+desc) # actually desc length +4 for width? But we compute via len(desc)+4
    all_names.append("Total")
    # compute width as max(len(name) for names)
    # But for desc we need len(desc)+4
    max_width=0
    for proj in proj_desc_minutes:
        max_width=max(max_width, len(proj))
        for desc in proj_desc_minutes[proj]:
            max_width=max(max_width, len(desc)+4)
    max_width=max(max_width, len("Total"))
    # If no projects, max_width is len("Total")=5
    # Then for each project header and description and total, pad with dots to width
    # Function to format line with dots
    def format_dotted(name, mins, is_total=False, is_project=False):
        dur=format_duration(mins)
        # name is already maybe with indent for desc? For project, name is proj, for desc, name is "    desc"
        # Determine base len
        base_len=len(name)
        dots_needed = max_width - base_len
        if dots_needed <0:
            dots_needed=0
        # But original for project with long name, if dots_needed==0, they use single space? In our earlier width calc, when project > max_width? but max_width is max, so dots_needed>=0; for equalling max, dots_needed=0 -> they use single space before duration
        # They still put one space before duration regardless of dots.
        if dots_needed==0:
            return f"{name} {dur}"
        else:
            return f"{name}{'.'*dots_needed} {dur}"
    # Sort projects alphabetically
    sorted_projects=sorted(proj_desc_minutes.keys())
    for proj in sorted_projects:
        # project total line bold
        line = format_dotted(proj, total_by_proj[proj], is_project=True)
        stdout_write(f"\x1b[1m{line}\x1b[0m\n")
        # sort descriptions alphabetically
        for desc in sorted(proj_desc_minutes[proj].keys()):
            mins=proj_desc_minutes[proj][desc]
            name="    "+desc
            line2=format_dotted(name, mins)
            stdout_write(f"{line2}\n")
        stdout_write("\n")
    # total line
    total_line=format_dotted("Total", total_all, is_total=True)
    stdout_write(f"\x1b[1m{total_line}\x1b[0m\n\n")

def escape_text(s):
    # escape backslash then pipe
    # replace \ with \\ then | with \|
    return s.replace("\\", "\\\\").replace("|", "\\|")

def split_escaped_pipe(line):
    # split on unescaped |
    segs = []
    cur = []
    i = 0
    n = len(line)
    while i < n:
        c = line[i]
        if c == "\\":
            if i+1 < n:
                cur.append(line[i+1])
                i += 2
            else:
                i += 1
        elif c == "|":
            segs.append(''.join(cur).strip())
            cur = []
            i += 1
        else:
            cur.append(c)
            i += 1
    segs.append(''.join(cur).strip())
    return segs

def parse_datetime_str(s):
    try:
        # format YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM
        return dt.strptime(s, "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
    except:
        return None

def format_datetime(d):
    return d.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")

def format_time(d):
    return d.strftime("%H:%M")

def format_duration(minutes):
    if minutes < 1:
        return "<1m"
    hours = minutes // 60
    mins = minutes % 60
    if hours == 0:
        return f"{mins:02d}m"
    else:
        return f"{hours}h {mins:02d}m"

def parse_date_str(s):
    # try YYYY-MM-DD
    try:
        return dt.strptime(s, "%Y-%m-%d").date()
    except:
        return None

def parse_time_arg(s):
    # returns datetime for today or None + error type
    # check contains invalid characters: if not matches pattern \d{1,2}:\d{2}
    # Actually check if string matches ^\d{1,2}:\d{2}$ else invalid characters
    if not re.match(r'^\d{1,2}:\d{2}$', s):
        return None, "invalid_chars"
    h, m = s.split(":")
    try:
        hi = int(h); mi = int(m)
    except:
        return None, "invalid_chars"
    if hi <0 or hi>23 or mi<0 or mi>59:
        return None, "out_of_range"
    # construct today datetime
    today = ddate.today()
    # use local now? We'll use today's date
    try:
        return dt.combine(today, dtime(hi, mi)), None
    except:
        return None, "out_of_range"

def parse_duration_str(s):
    # expects number + m or h
    if len(s) < 2:
        return None
    suffix = s[-1]
    if suffix not in ('m','h'):
        return None
    num = s[:-1]
    if not num.isdigit():
        return None
    try:
        n = int(num)
    except:
        return None
    if suffix == 'm':
        return n
    else:
        return n*60

def round_datetime(d, round_minutes):
    if round_minutes is None or round_minutes == 0:
        return d
    # compute minutes since midnight
    minutes = d.hour*60 + d.minute
    # round to nearest
    # using half up
    rounded = int(minutes / round_minutes + 0.5) * round_minutes
    # handle overflow to next day
    days_add = rounded // 1440
    rounded_minutes = rounded % 1440
    new_hour = rounded_minutes // 60
    new_min = rounded_minutes % 60
    new_date = d.date() + timedelta(days=days_add)
    # preserve seconds 0
    return dt.combine(new_date, dtime(new_hour, new_min))

    activities = []
    errors = [] # list of (line_no, line_content, error_type)
    # error_type: "activity" or "date"
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        return None, None, "not_found"
    try:
        with open(path, 'r', encoding='utf-8', errors='replace') as f:
            lines = f.readlines()
    except Exception as e:
        return None, None, str(e)
    for idx, raw in enumerate(lines, start=1):
        line = raw.rstrip('\n')
        # skip? But blank line is error per earlier? We'll treat blank as error.
        # Need to decide: if line.strip() == "" then it's activity parse error
        if line.strip() == "":
            errors.append((idx, line, "activity"))
            continue
        # check if contains unescaped pipe at all? Use split_escaped_pipe to detect
        # quick check: does line contain '|' not escaped? We'll use our split logic to see number of segments
        # If line has no '|' character at all, then activity error
        # Actually our split will return 1 segment if no '|', but we can detect
        # We'll attempt to parse
        segs = split_escaped_pipe(line)
        if len(segs) < 2:
            # need at least date and project?
            # But earlier we saw single pipe line with 2 segments succeeded. So at least 2 segments (1 pipe) yields attempt date parse.
            # If only 1 segment, then activity error
            errors.append((idx, line, "activity"))
            continue
        date_part = segs[0]
        # date_part may contain " - "
        if " - " in date_part:
            parts = date_part.split(" - ", 1)
            start_str = parts[0].strip()
            end_str = parts[1].strip()
            start_dt = parse_datetime_str(start_str)
            end_dt = parse_datetime_str(end_str)
            if start_dt is None or end_dt is None:
                errors.append((idx, line, "date"))
                continue
        else:
            start_dt = parse_datetime_str(date_part.strip())
            if start_dt is None:
                errors.append((idx, line, "date"))
                continue
            end_dt = None
        # project and description
        project = segs[1] if len(segs) >=2 else ""
        description = segs[2] if len(segs) >=3 else ""
        # For extra pipes, ignore rest (already handled by taking only first three, but our segs for 4+ will have extra)
        # If there are more than 3 segments, description is segs[2] (already) and we ignore rest? That's what original does.
        activities.append({
            "start": start_dt,
            "end": end_dt,
            "project": project,
            "description": description,
            "line_no": idx,
            "raw": line,
        })
    return activities, errors, None

            # duration = start_dt - act["start"] if positive else 0
